oneliner: One angle-of-attack sensor glitched, so the automation kept pushing the nose down — and the pilots couldn't out-trim it.
summary: MCAS trimmed the stabilizer nose-down based on a SINGLE angle-of-attack sensor. A faulty sensor made it fire repeatedly, with more authority than the pilots' counter-trim, re-triggering each time they responded. Certification assumed crews would diagnose it as ordinary runaway trim within seconds; training was minimized to keep a common type rating. Lion Air 610 and Ethiopian 302 were lost. No single broken part explains it: a sensor fault + single-sensor authority + hidden system + training economics + certification assumptions.
source: US House T&I Committee Final Report (2020); JATR (2019)
